additions.reason: CurrentEN offers only 'control, management', which against 警察がスピード違反の取り締まりを行っている reads as administration or paperwork, not police enforcement — a learner would picture the traffic bureau filing reports rather than stopping speeders. The Chinese list already carries the sense (取缔); only the English lacks it, the pattern behind most accepted gaps so far. Reading and transitivity check clean: this is the noun of the transitive 取り締まる at とりしまり, no partner-verb or homophone leak.

CurrentEN gives only the abstract 'blood relationship', so the gloss line beside 唯一の肉親を探している yields 'searching for his only blood relationship' — the word here denotes a person, not a relation, and the learner is left guessing. The Chinese already carries the personal sense (骨肉亲人 names people); only the English is missing it. 肉親/にくしん has no competing reading and no transitive partner, so the only question was person-vs-relation, and the sentence needs the person.

失敗を誤魔化す is the evade/cover-up sense, not the deceive-a-person or falsify-figures sense. 'to deceive, to falsify, to misrepresent' produces nonsense on this sentence ('he deceived his mistake'), and the Chinese 敷衍/欺骗 does not give 掩饰 either — so both halves of the gloss line fail here. Reading ごまかす is right and the verb stays transitive, so no partner-verb hazard.

The normative use, above all the very common negative 好ましくない ("inadvisable, undesirable"), is not reachable from "nice, pleasant" — a learner would read 感情的になるのは好ましくない as "becoming emotional is not pleasant", a claim about enjoyment rather than about what one should do. The Chinese line half-carries it via 令人满意的, but neither language states the advisability sense outright, so this one is a gap in both.

The transitive Xを慎む ("refrain from X, abstain from") is the sense the sentence needs, and "to be careful, to be chaste" would send a learner to "one should be careful with selfish remarks" — an admonition to do it carefully rather than not at all. The Chinese list already carries the sense via 节制; only the English lacks it. Checked that this is つつしむ, not the 謹む honorific-humility spelling's separate use.

Reading check (failure mode 3): 強請る has two readings — ゆする 'to extort, to blackmail' and ねだる 'to beg, to pester, to coax'. The card's kana is ねだる, but currentEN 'to extort, to demand' is the ゆする entry. A learner seeing 妹は誕生日に新しいバッグを強請った beside 'to extort' would read it as the sister extorting a bag. The Chinese list partly carries the right sense already (死乞白赖地要 = to whine/pester for), so this is mainly an English-side gap.

The English line 'incomplete understanding, doubt' names only the internal feeling of doubt, never the outward-facing 'suspicious, arousing suspicion' use that dominates real usage (不審な行動, 不審者). A learner reading 'his incomplete-understanding behavior / his doubt behavior' would not get 彼の不審な行動. This is an English-only gap: the Chinese list already carries it as 可疑.

弁論大会 is a speech contest — one speaker delivering a prepared address (Daijirin's first sense: 大勢の前で自分の意見を述べること). The card offers only 'discussion, debate, argument' and ZH only 辩论, so here the Chinese does NOT already carry it — both lists are short. A learner reading 辩论 beside 高校生の弁論大会 would picture a two-sided debate tournament and get the sentence wrong, which is the misunderstanding bar. Reading べんろん is correct and the sense lives at it.

食べ物を恵む is the give-in-charity sense (JMdict's separate 'to give, to donate' sense); 'to bless / to show mercy to' leaves a learner unable to parse 'give food to the needy'. The Chinese list already carries it as 施舍 — only the English lacks it, so the ZH gloss is a duplicate and may be dropped.

うんざり names the experiencer's state (待ち時間にはうんざりした = I got fed up), but the English line gives only stimulus adjectives 'tedious, boring' — a learner cannot get 'I got fed up' out of that, and could not produce the sentence. The Chinese 厌烦/腻烦 already carries the sense, so this is an English-only gap and the ZH gloss is redundant.

きちっと has a tidiness sense (きちっと整理する, きちっとした身なり) distinct from the precision sense; 'exactly, perfectly' reads as accuracy and would make きちっとした服装 come out as 'exact clothing'. The Chinese list already carries it as 整洁 — only the English lacks it.

要求を退ける is the reject/turn-down sense, distinct from physically repelling an enemy; 'to repel, to drive away' would give a learner 'drove away the demand'. Reading checks out — this sense lives at しりぞける, not どける/のける. The Chinese list already has 拒绝, so only the English is missing it (the ZH 退却 is in fact the intransitive 退く, worth a separate cleanup).

Dictionaries split 他方 into a noun ('one of two, the other side') and an adverbial/conjunctive 〜する他方で 'on the other hand, meanwhile'. The evidence sentence is the second, and 'another side, different direction' reads as a physical/positional noun there — a learner would try to parse 励む他方で as 'a different direction'. The Chinese list already carries the sense (另一方面 is precisely the connective); only the English lacks it.

refused.why:
驳回。提案属于"给句型上词义"的失败模式，而非 currentEN 真正够不到的义项。

1) 不是独立义项。日语单语辞典（大辞林・大辞泉一系）把「類のない美しさ」直接放在「同じ程度・種類のもの」这一条下面作例句，并不另立"匹敌者"义。也就是说，"without equal"是否定式 ～のない 在英语里的归化译法，不是 たぐい 本身多出来的一层意思。该词在肯定句里从不表示"同辈/匹敌者"：说不出 彼は私の類だ 来表示"他是我的对手"。理由中列举的 類のない／類まれ／類を見ない 全部是否定极性或近乎固化的搭配，提案把搭配义提升成词义，多走了一步。

2) 现有英文并未失守。由 kind/sort/type 得到 "no other of its kind"，学习者已经落在正确语义上；"a talent with no other kind" 是逐字套词表的产物，而这条标准并未用于该词表的其他条目。evidenceZH 的"无可比拟"同理，是句式的成品译文，不能反过来证明 类 缺义。

3) 形式不合格。"equal, match" 以裸名词形式排在三个类别名词之后，会被读成第四个"种类"义；且 equal 单独出现在名词/形容词/动词之间无从判别。因实质不成立，不给改写版。

补充（供上级判断，未作为论据）：提案称 類を見ない 属 たぐい 读音，但该惯用语在 たぐい 与 るい 之间读法存在实际分歧，不足以承重，故未采用。反之，提案关于"本卡是 たぐい 而非 るい（class, genus）"的判断是正确的，读音错配这一常见失败模式在此不成立——驳回不依赖该点。

驳回。理由三条，任一即足以否决：

1) 现有英文列表已经覆盖该义。本場 是地点名词，只有一个核心义：某事物的本源之地、因而是最地道的地方。英语 "home" 恰好带这层含义（the home of jazz / the home of Neapolitan pizza），学习者用 "home" 读 本場のイタリア料理 得到 "Italian food from its home"，正是 authentic 的读法；"center" 亦从另一侧覆盖（the center of X）。这不是勉强的覆盖，是英语该词自带的引申。

2) 提案描述的是例句译文，不是词义。本場 本身没有第二个义项；"authentic" 是 〜の 定语用法在英译时被迫采用的形容词化处理。给名词加一个只在特定句法环境下浮现的译法，等于把例句写进词条。

3) 形式不合。currentEN 三项皆为名词（home / habitat / center），插入光杆形容词 "authentic" 造成词性不齐，且会误导学习者把 本場 当作形容词性词（如误造 *本場だ / *本場な）。提案 JSON 里的 proposedSense 写作 "authentic place of origin"（名词短语），与 reviewer 实际提交的 gloss "authentic"（形容词）本身就不一致——名词短语版本又与 "home" 完全重复。

中文列表已有 正宗 不构成英文缺口的证据：正宗 在中文里本身兼作名词与定语，中英两列无需一一对应。属于「看似合理但英文并未真正够不到」的情形，按默认驳回。

Refuted — the existing English already reaches this, and the proposed wording would misdirect.

1) Same sense, not a new one. 甘口 is one scalar term: the 甘い pole of the 甘口⇔中辛⇔辛口 axis. Japanese monolingual dictionaries give only 甘みの多いこと (sake, miso, and by extension any product graded on that axis) plus 甘い物好き and 甘言 — there is no separate 'mild' entry. The curry grade is that single sense applied to a food whose opposite pole happens to be 辛い-hot rather than 辛い-dry. currentEN 'sweet flavor' already names that pole, and it is not even factually wrong on a curry box: 甘口カレー is genuinely sweetened (apple, honey) and is labelled 甘口 for exactly that reason.

2) The proposal describes the evidence sentence, not the word. The reviewer's argument is entirely about how 甘口 reads on 甘口のカレー ('least-spicy grade'). 'Least-spicy grade' is what the 甘口/中辛/辛口 scale does to the word in one product category — packaging semantics, not a lexical sense. Nothing about 甘口 in isolation means 'mild'; strip the curry and 'mild flavor' is unusable.

3) The proposed gloss is badly formed, and its defect is not repairable by rewording — which is why this is a refusal rather than an upheld-with-better-EN. English 'mild flavor' means faint or subtle taste. 甘口 never means that; a 甘口 curry is strongly flavoured, just not hot. Adding 'mild flavor' next to 'sweet flavor' would teach a second wrong reading while claiming to fix the first. The only accurate English is a qualifier on the existing item ('sweet flavor (of curry etc., mild rather than hot)'), i.e. a parenthetical, not a new list entry — and that is a different proposal from the one under review.

4) The ZH argument does not rescue it. The evidence ZH wrote 微甜不辣 because that is a sentence translation doing contextual work ('sweet-ish, not spicy'), which is precisely what a translator does with a scalar term in context. That a sentence gloss is longer than the headword gloss is normal, not evidence of a missing sense; currentZH 甜味 sits on the same axis as 甜味/辣味 and covers it.

Checked the three known triage escapes: no alternative reading (あまくち is the only reading in use; かんこう is not this word), no transitive/intransitive partner (nominal, not a verb), and no homophone in different kanji competing for this slot. None applies — the proposal fails on redundancy and wording, not on a reading confusion.

Refuted on two grounds. (1) The current English already reaches the sense: the list is "class, group, category", and "group" is an ordinary English word for an organizational unit inside a company (the development group, a product group). 開発部門の責任者 renders fine as "head of the development group". The reviewer's "head of the development category" argument works only by picking the worst gloss on the list and ignoring the one that carries the organizational reading — and the rule is to refute when the English covers the sense even loosely or in other words. (2) 部門 is one sense, not two: "a division of a larger whole". Whether the whole is a contest (entry categories) or a company (development division), the word does not change meaning, only the context does. So "department or division" describes the evidence sentence 彼は開発部門の責任者として働いている rather than a sense the word has and the list lacks. Checked the three standing failure modes and none applies (ぶもん is the only reading of 部門; it is a noun with no transitive/intransitive partner; no common ぶもん homophone in other kanji) — the proposal fails on coverage instead. The supporting arguments do not carry: 部门 is the direct Chinese cognate of the compound, so ZH/EN parity is not evidence of an English gap, and the 特定 precedent is a different shape (there the added sense was unreachable from the existing glosses; here it is one hop from "group"). Separately, "department or division" is malformed for a card line — two glosses fused with "or" where every other item is a single bare noun.
